MVR GDTF download queue lifecycle

gui/gdtf_download_queue_dialog.{h,cpp} owns widgets, row presentation, summary/progress formatting, cancellation requests and terminal acknowledgement. The importer owns catalog loading, matching, source selection, reuse and fallback assignment. No matching, conflict policy or serialization rules change.

mvr::preferences::kAutoCloseGdtfDownloadWindowKey uses the existing user preference store (user_config.json). Only 1 enables automatic dismissal; missing and invalid values keep the queue visible. The Preferences container commits the page's staged edits using its existing save service. Credentials remain a separate concern. Headless workflows do not consume this GUI policy.

The synchronous importer enters one standard wxWidgets modal dialog before starting the queue. A dialog-owned one-shot event starts the existing workflow; completion enables OK and either awaits acknowledgement or ends that same modal boundary. There is no second completion dialog, manual wait loop, or new yield checkpoint. While active, OK is ignored and close/Escape requests cancellation without destroying the stack-owned dialog. After work returns, cancellation is terminal and the normal completion preference applies. Exceptions unwind through the modal boundary and are rethrown to the caller. The dialog is explicitly hidden after the modal call returns, before resuming import or rethrowing an exception, to normalize native-port visibility on macOS as well as other ports. Progress callbacks remain synchronous and are not posted to a window after its lifetime ends.

Existing limitations and future shared workflow

Network requests still run synchronously, and existing import yield checkpoints remain. Cancellation responsiveness during an individual blocking HTTP transfer is limited by that existing design. This change does not add worker-thread UI access or additional yield-based waiting. The modal boundary disables its parent while the queue runs and prevents premature resumption of conflict assignment.

A later Core service could own an immutable queue request, per-item resolution results, transferred/total bytes, cancellation token and structured completion and diagnostic events. The existing GDTF Share client already exposes structured transfer progress and result categories; those values can feed GUI, CLI and future MCP/AI adapters. Importer-specific catalog/matching orchestration still uses wx strings, logging and fixture assignment and is not yet such a service. GUI labels, colors, dialog acknowledgement and automatic window closing must remain in GUI adapters. No new CLI command or Core GUI dependency is introduced.
